summary: PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 is a careful extraction, and its 19 source issues stand. I recomputed E5, E6, E8, E10, E13 and E15 and read the others at their locators. The published paper (hash as recorded) has no correction. The known withdrawal is of the sequel EVW II, whose gap Ellenberg traces to combining this paper's operator U with the sequel's V, and the extraction records that correctly. There are 16 findings: 9 medium and 7 low. Medium: (1) and (2) the routes contain cycles: IG items /15, /16, /65 depend on Part II items /10, /12, /14, and IG item /137 depends on ArithmeticStatistics item /100 while ArithmeticStatistics depends on IG. (3) The Hurwitz action, the Hurwitz covering spaces and the braid-orbit monoid are re-planned in the Part II, although IG.3 and IG.5 own them and Wood 19/255 routed the monoid to IG.3 a day earlier. (4) Proposition 7.8's comparison half duplicates Wood 19/86 and /259 at IG.5. (5) The punctured-disc mapping class group duplicates Landesman–Litt 24's new mapping-class roadmap and Tau Ceti GeometricTopology Layer 3. (7) Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layers 3 and 10 already plan the Cl(O_L) ≅ Pic⁰ bridge and the y² = f(x) genus formula. (8) The Artin comparison and the SGA 1 XII π_1 comparison have no items. (9) The Katz–Lang/Kummer classification of A-covers by Jac[ℓ^k] has no item or prerequisite. (11) A missed source issue: the published abstract and the sentence after Theorem 1.2 claim the result for all large q, but the proof fails for q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ); for A = (Z/ℓ)² there are ℓ rational components. Low: Tau Ceti asphericity API uncited (6); the GSp_q lifting step (10); a Proposition 4.13 misprint (12); a wrong locator introduced by the review (13); horizontal tameness duplicated with Klevdal–Patrikis 25 (14); sourceVersions and register attribution of E15–E19 (15); the report out of sync with the result (16). Disclosure: this session wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-74/80 and red-teamed Browning–Sawin 20 and Koymans–Pagano. No finding relies on them, and the configuration-space overlap raised in RT-PAPER-BROWNING-SAWIN-20/3 is not repeated.

Source, version of record. Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), no. 3, 729–786, https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n3-p01-p.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026: 759,582 bytes, SHA-256 6c10d770348c625ad9fe80d2c47093cde2a2ba05f39a28d547743f0f4993a7f6, the extraction's hash. I read it in full (§§1–8 and the references) through pdftotext, and rendered pp. 729 and 754 to check the abstract and Proposition 4.13. Also arXiv:0912.0325v4 (1 December 2015; SHA-256 4adef21f…, as the ArithmeticStatistics packet records it) for its abstract.

Versions and published corrections, checked 30 September 2026. The arXiv listing of 0912.0325 has v1 (2 December 2009), v2 (3 December 2009, 'bibliography accidentally absent from v1'), v3 (2 July 2014, 'Substantial edits of sections 1-6') and v4 (1 December 2015, 'Final version; to appear in Annals'); none is withdrawn. The known withdrawal is of the sequel, arXiv:1212.0923 (v2, 19 November 2013, 'temporarily withdrawn owing to a gap ... the homological stabilization maps used in this paper and the previous paper are not exactly the same'). Ellenberg's post of 23 November 2013 (https://quomodocumque.wordpress.com/2013/11/23/homological-stability-for-hurwitz-spaces-ii-temporarily-withdrawn/) says the error, found by Randal-Williams, is in combining this paper's operator U with the sequel's V: 'We prove (and there is no problem here) that U is an isomorphism ... the main theorems of both papers are correct'. Landesman–Levy (arXiv:2410.22210, footnote in §1.3) describe it the same way. Landesman–Levy arXiv:2503.03861 cites EVW16's Theorem 6.1 argument without correction. So the extraction is right that this paper carries no correction. Its Part II brief already says to build the stability theorem 'with its actual central operator U', which is the lesson of the EVW II gap.

All 137 items (7 library, 8 planned, 122 missing), the 3 routes and their briefs, the 11 prerequisites, the remainingWork and remainingWorkStatus, and all 19 sourceIssues with their review verdicts. Every missing item is routed exactly once (53 + 23 + 46 = 122). Every cross-route dependsOn edge was listed. That is how findings 1 and 2 were found: 15, 16 and 65 depend on route-1 items, and 137 on route-3 item 100.

Source issues rechecked. E6: I enumerated X = C9×C3, A = C3², A′ = C9×C3. There are 48 surjections X ↠ A, 12 of which lift, and 108 surjections X ↠ A′, so the aggregate inequality 108 ≥ 2·48 holds. E15: the subgroup of SL2(Z/9) generated by [[0,1],[8,0]] and [[1,7],[6,7]] has order 24 and maps injectively onto SL2(F3). E5: for x of exact monodromy Q, r_g^{D|g|}x with g ∉ Q lies in a larger-monodromy summand, so U ≡ U_Q, with coefficient 1. E8: squarefree polynomials of degree 1 number q, giving |S_1| = 2q. E10: σ acts on Cl as −1, so (L,α) ≅ (L,−α), and −I ∈ Sp(V) keeps the orbit count. E13: ∏(1−3^{−i}) ≈ 0.5601. E2, E3, E4, E9, E11, E12 and E14 were read at their locators and stand. E11: the Kummer parametrization and the tame A⋊Z/2 theory exclude characteristic 2, and §8 excludes ℓ | q. E1 and E7 stand. E16–E19, on Achter–Pries and Vasiu, were checked for mathematical soundness (the μ2-gerbe of the labelled hyperelliptic stack; the exact multiplier sequence; the commutator in a single dual-number kernel being trivial; locally free against free Lie modules), but I did not reread those sources.

The paper's arguments re-derived. The induction degree bookkeeping (6.1.4)–(6.1.5), the ranges needed for Proposition 5.1's p+q < n−2, Theorem 4.2 from Lemmas 4.6–4.9 and Propositions 4.10–4.13 (including A0 ≥ 5A1+1), Lemma 3.5's filtration argument, the estimate (8.8.3) and /95's closed form C²/(√q − C), Lemma 8.9's decomposition and orthogonality, and the GSp_q lift of finding 10. For q ≡ −1 (mod ℓ) nothing is excluded: Lemma 8.9 needs only q ≢ 1, and the extraction does not wrongly exclude it. The q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ) orbit count of finding 11 was checked for A = (Z/ℓ)².

Library claims. All 15 cited declarations exist at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 (declarations.tsv: AlgebraicTopology.singularChainComplexFunctor and singularHomologyFunctor, TauCeti.BraidGroup and .lift, Quandle.Conj and conj_act_eq_conj, MonoidAlgebra and .lift, CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence, SemidirectProduct with inl, inr and rightHom, Matrix.symplecticGroup and SymplecticGroup.mem_iff). I searched declarations.tsv for Hurwitz, braid, configuration, quandle, nonsplit, Cohen–Lenstra, GSp, similitude, Weil pairing, Salvetti, arc complex, semisimplicial, asphericity, Eilenberg–MacLane, punctured, Nakayama, hyperelliptic, isotropic, Lagrangian, Tor, leftDerived, spectral sequence, group homology, coinvariants, CW complex, Lefschetz and squarefree counts. This found the Tau Ceti asphericity and K(G,1) API (finding 6). Tau Ceti's SymplecticForm.IsLagrangian is over ℝ only, so it does not serve /102–/103 over Z_ℓ. There is no noncommutative Tor: Mathlib's TensorProduct needs a commutative ring, and only Functor.leftDerived exists. So the extraction's 'missing' statuses for §4 stand.

Planned statuses. I read the atlas text of FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4 (/85), EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings (/91), DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7 (/92), SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 with the UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting externals, whose integration owner is SF.2 (/93; the review's observation stands), Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stages 4 and 5 as the review quotes them (/111, /112), AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4 (/126) and IG.0 (/127). Each plans its item in the paper's generality. I also read IG.0–IG.6 and ST.0–ST.5, the Tau Ceti READMEs of AlgebraicCurves (Layers 3 and 10), GeometricTopology (Layer 3 and the inventory), UniversalCovers (Stage 4), BelyiMaps and JacobianChallenge (Albanese), and EDC.6 and the ComplexComparisonPartII stages for comparison theorems.

findings.claim: The routes create a dependency cycle. Route 1 is a Part II whose parent, and first prerequisite, is InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups. Yet three items routed by route 2 into that parent's own stages (IG.0, IG.1, IG.3, IG.5) depend on items routed into the Part II: /15 (marked topological branched G-cover) depends on /12; /16 (topological monodromy classification) depends on /10 and /14; /65 (rational conjugacy-class locus, whose complex points are CHur^c/G) depends on /14. Applying both routes makes IG import the Part II, which imports IG. The review checked only that the 243 item-level edges are acyclic; it did not check the edges between routes.

findings.claim: Route 1 plans the Hurwitz action on tuples, the Hurwitz covering spaces and their Nielsen, boundary and global monodromy invariants, and the monoid of braid orbits with its central stabilizer, all in the new Part II. It justifies this with 'IG.3 and IG.5 plan branch cycles, descent, Hurwitz moduli and specialization, but not the chain-level nonsplitting stability argument of EVW §§3–6'. That is true of §§4–6. But IG.3 plans 'the braid action' on generating tuples and IG.5 plans 'Hurwitz moduli with braid/Nielsen-class components', and two extractions accepted a day earlier route the same objects there. PAPER-WOOD-19/255 (route 5, IG.3) plans the monoid of braid orbits of c-tuples, a central power-block element and bijectivity of multiplication by it in high multiplicity, which is EVW §3.3 and the first half of Lemma 3.5 (/22, /25, /26). Its input, Fried–Völklein's appendix Lemma 3, is EVW Proposition 3.4 (/24, whose proof cites the same appendix [27]). PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24 route 2 routes its Hurwitz-space vocabulary to IG.5, and says explicitly that EVW does the same. The atlas would build the braid monoid and the Hurwitz action twice, once for tuples with product one and once for arbitrary tuples.

findings.claim: Item /69 (Proposition 7.8, uniform étale Betti bound) is routed to the Part II as a single item. Its first half, the comparison (7.8.2) H^i(Hn^c(ℂ), Z/ℓ) ≅ H^i_ét(Hn^c/F̄_q, Z/ℓ) for ℓ > n, obtained from Proposition 7.7 on the ordered pullback and then S_n-invariants, is the theorem that PAPER-WOOD-19 routes to IG.5 as /86 and /259, citing EVW Proposition 7.7. The Part II's brief says to 'Import arithmetic Hurwitz schemes and tame comparison from IG.5', but the item itself does not separate the comparison from the stability step, so the Part II would rebuild it.

Thus, supposing ℓ > n, we obtain an isomorphism (7.8.2) H^i(Hn^c_{G,n}(ℂ), Z/ℓZ) ≅ H^i_ét(Hn^c_{G,n}/F̄_q, Z/ℓZ).' findings.claim: Items /9 (Conf_n(D) is a K(B_n,1)) and /13 (the Hurwitz spaces are finite covers of Conf_n with the Borel homotopy type) are 'missing' with no library citation. Tau Ceti at the pin has the vocabulary and the covering-space transfer they need: IsAspherical, IsEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne, and the theorem that a path-connected cover of an aspherical space is a K(H,1) for the image H of its fundamental group. The last is exactly EVW's statement in §1.3 that each component of a Hurwitz space is aspherical with fundamental group a subgroup of B_n, which has no item. What remains missing is the asphericity of Conf_n itself (EVW footnote 5, the Fadell–Neuwirth fibration argument).

findings.claim: The paper uses two comparison theorems between algebraic and topological invariants over ℂ, and no item states either. (a) Artin's comparison theorem between étale and singular cohomology with finite coefficients (SGA 4 XI, Th. 4.4) turns Proposition 7.7's étale statement into the isomorphism with the cohomology of the complex Hurwitz space in Proposition 7.8. (b) The comparison of étale and topological fundamental groups (SGA 1 XII, Th. 5.1, Riemann existence) gives Lemma 7.4, H(ℂ) ≅ CHur/G; item /65 merely asserts the conclusion, 'Over C, its analytic space is CHur^c_G,n/G'. Route 2's reason says only 'Import Riemann existence ... from their established owners', and the prerequisites list SGA 1 XII–XIII but not SGA 4 XI. Without items, nothing records the owners or the hypotheses (finite coefficients, finite type over ℂ).

findings.claim: In the proof of Theorem 8.8, the generic fibre of X_n → Conf_n is identified with Sur(V, A) (corrected to Sur(V, A)/±1 by E10) using the fact that abelian étale covers of a curve C over an algebraically closed field with group A, ℓ^k A = 0, are classified by surjections Jac(C)[ℓ^k] ↠ A. EVW cite Katz–Lang [37, (2.4)] for it. This is the geometric replacement for the class-field step (8.7.2) and is the only link between the Hurwitz fibre and the symplectic module V. No item states it: /97 depends on /84, /87 and /96, and /96 constructs V but not the classification. Katz–Lang is not in the prerequisites. remainingWork mentions an open 'Jacobian/Kummer ... dictionary' without planning it.

findings.claim: The reduction of the finite-level orbit question to Lemma 8.9, which is stated for the ℓ-adic lattice, has no item. It needs two facts: Sur(V, A) = Sur(T, A) when ℓ^k A = 0, and surjectivity of GSp_q(T) → GSp_q(T/ℓ^k), so that a finite-level similitude fixing f lifts to one on T. /135 records only the surjectivity of the integral symplectic group onto Sp at finite level, and /106 says only 'Combine full hyperelliptic monodromy, the corrected generic fibre and the unique stable orbit theorem'. The step is true: GSp_q(T) contains diag(q·1_g, 1_g) in a symplectic basis, so GSp_q(T/ℓ^k) = h̄_0·Sp(T/ℓ^k), and Sp(T) → Sp(T/ℓ^k) is onto because Sp is smooth over Z_ℓ.
findings.evidence: EVW p. 780: 'Write T for the full Tate module of Jac(C), so that T/ℓ^k ≃ V. Because we chose k so that ℓ^k A = 0, the pullback under T → V identifies Sur(V, A) → Sur(T, A). By smoothness, the map GSpq(T) → GSpq(V) is surjective. Therefore, our desired conclusion follows from the subsequent lemma.' /135: 'The integral symplectic group surjects to every finite level by smoothness'.
findings.fix: Add an item 'Finite-level reduction to the lattice' (Theorem 8.8 proof, p. 780) stating both facts with the proof above, in route 3. Make /106 depend on it and on /105.

findings.claim: The published abstract, and the sentence after Theorem 1.2, state the arithmetic consequence for every q > Q, without Theorem 1.2's restriction q ≢ 1 (mod ℓ). The paper proves it only for q ≢ 1 (mod ℓ) (odd, prime to ℓ, per E11). For q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ) it says only that 'the method of proof still works' and yields a different distribution, and gives no argument. The method does not go through verbatim. Take A = (Z/ℓ)² and q ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), k = 1. Then GSp_q(V) = Sp(V) contains the identity, so every Sp(V)-orbit on Sur(V, A) is Frobenius-stable. These orbits are separated by the value ω(f_1*, f_2*) ∈ F_ℓ of the pairing on the dual pair, so there are ℓ of them, each stable under −I. So there are ℓ rational components, and the A-moment tends to ℓ, not 1. Proposition 8.3 then does not apply, and the paper proves no replacement. E11 records only the characteristic-2 and characteristic-ℓ part of the domain. Item /110 silently narrows to 'allowed q'. No finding records the broader printed claims.
findings.evidence: Annals p. 729, Abstract (published PDF, SHA-256 6c10d770…, rendered and read): 'Then there exists Q = Q(A) such that, for q greater than Q, a positive fraction of quadratic extensions of Fq(t) have the ℓ-part of their class group isomorphic to A.' The same wording is in the arXiv v4 PDF. The arXiv abstract page of every version, v1 (2 December 2009) to v4 (1 December 2015), reads '... for q greater than Q and not congruent to 1 modulo l, a positive fraction ...'. p. 730, after Theorem 1.2: 'When q = 1 (mod ℓ), the method of proof still works; for any fixed positive ℓ-valuation of q − 1, the proof yields a distribution that differs from the Cohen-Lenstra distribution ... In particular, for q > Q0(ℓ), a positive fraction of imaginary quadratic extensions of Fq(t) have class number divisible by ℓ, and a positive fraction have class number indivisible by ℓ.' p. 780, Lemma 8.9: 'q ∈ Z_ℓ^× be such that q − 1 is invertible in Z_ℓ'.

findings.claim: Proposition 4.13 is printed with a misplaced parenthesis: 'max(deg(H_0(M)), deg(H_1(M)) + A_1q + (4A_1 + A_2)' closes the max only at the end, which would read as max(deg H_0, deg H_1 + A_1 q + 4A_1 + A_2). This is a different bound, and it gives nothing linear in q for the H_0 term. The proof's display, max(deg H_0(M), deg H_1(M)) + (A_2 + q − i) + A_1 i + 4A_1, shows the intended max(deg H_0(M), deg H_1(M)) + A_1 q + 4A_1 + A_2. Item /43 states the intended form but no finding records the misprint.

findings.claim: The review changed /51's locator from 'Proposition 5.4 via 5.6' to 'Lemma 5.4 via Proposition 5.6'. Lemma 5.4 is not the connectivity statement.
